{{< include _controls.qmd >}}

```{ojs}
//| output: false
mixedCurrency = currency === "Local" && trendCountry === "All countries"
effectiveTrendMode = mixedCurrency && trendMode === "price" ? "change" : trendMode
// Per gallon and per litre differ by a constant, so on a percentage axis they
// draw the same lines. Dimmed rather than explained in a sentence under the
// chart; it still sets the prices in the tooltip, which is why it is not
// disabled outright.
volumeGuard = {
  const inert = effectiveTrendMode === "change";
  for (const input of (viewof volume).querySelectorAll("input")) {
    const label = input.closest("label");
    if (label) {
      label.title = inert ? "A percentage axis is the same per gallon and per litre" : "";
      label.classList.toggle("cgp-option-off", inert);
    }
  }
  return inert;
}

trendModeGuard = {
  const input = (viewof trendMode).querySelector('input[data-value="price"]');
  if (input) {
    input.disabled = mixedCurrency;
    const label = input.closest("label");
    if (label) {
      label.title = mixedCurrency ? "One price axis needs one currency" : "";
      label.classList.toggle("cgp-option-off", mixedCurrency);
    }
  }
  return mixedCurrency;
}

// The card body is laid out after the cell runs, and Leaflet needs a real size.
trendRegionRows =
  db && trendCountry !== "All countries"
    ? db.query(`
        SELECT region,
               brand,
               strftime(capture_date, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d,
               n_stations,
               median_local_per_litre,
               median_usd_per_litre
        FROM summary_daily
        WHERE level = 'region'
          AND country = ${sqlText(trendCountry)}
          AND grade = ${sqlText(grade)}
        ORDER BY region, brand, capture_date
      `)
    : []
// A region's count is each chain's largest day, added up. The larger chain
// alone labelled a state both chains serve with half of its stations.
trendRegionOptions = {
  const perChain = new Map();
  for (const row of trendRegionRows) {
    const key = `${row.region} :: ${row.brand}`;
    const seen = perChain.get(key);
    if (row.n_stations > (seen ? seen.n : 0)) {
      perChain.set(key, {region: row.region, n: row.n_stations});
    }
  }
  const counts = new Map();
  for (const {region, n} of perChain.values()) counts.set(region, (counts.get(region) || 0) + n);
  return [...counts.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1] || (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : 1));
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof showBand = asField(
  Inputs.toggle({label: "Band: middle half of stations", value: true}),
  {inline: true}
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Static labels on purpose: if this depended on the breakdown or the currency,
// OJS would rebuild the node and reset the reader's choice every time either
// moved.
viewof trendMode = radioControl(
  "trendmode",
  [["Price", "price"], ["Change", "change"], ["Separate charts", "separate"]],
  "price",
  "View"
)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
viewof trendRegions = {
  const options = trendRegionOptions;
  const input = Inputs.checkbox(
    options.map((entry) => entry[0]),
    {
      label: "Regions",
      value: options.slice(0, PALETTE_SERIES_CAP).map((entry) => entry[0]),
      format: (code) => {
        const found = options.find((entry) => entry[0] === code);
        return `${code} (${found ? found[1] : 0})`;
      }
    }
  );
  // Only a country breakdown has regions to pick from; with "All countries"
  // selected there is nothing to show, so the control stands down rather than
  // rendering an empty box.
  if (!options.length) input.style.display = "none";
  return asField(input);
}
```

```{ojs}
// Quarto gives every chunk its own card body, so three chunks stack down the
// card however short it is. Placing the controls in one chunk lets them sit on
// a single row -- which is all the height they need.
html`<div class="cgp-controls-row">${[
  viewof trendCountry,
  viewof trendMode,
  viewof showBand,
  viewof trendRegions
]}</div>`
```

## Price over time
::: {.cgp-panel .cgp-chart-card}

```{ojs}
// How many stations stood behind each day's median, as a strip under the chart
// rather than a sentence beside it. `n_stations` is already queried and was
// drawn nowhere, so a reader could not tell a real price move from a day when
// half the stations were missing.
function coverageStrip(rows, {label}) {
  const byDay = new Map();
  for (const row of rows) {
    const key = `${row.d} :: ${row.brand || ""}`;
    byDay.set(key, {
      day: toDay(row.d),
      brand: row.brand,
      series: row.brand ? `${row.country}-${row.brand}` : row.country,
      country: row.country,
      n: Number(row.n_stations) || 0
    });
  }
  const data = [...byDay.values()];
  if (data.length < 2) return "";
  return Plot.plot({
    width: chartWidth,
    // Deliberately not "open stations": a dip is usually a collection failure,
    // not a closure, and the two read very differently.
    ariaLabel: `Stations that posted a ${label} price, by day`,
    height: 70,
    marginLeft: 52,
    marginRight: 80,
    marginBottom: 22,
    style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
    x: {label: null, grid: false, ticks: 4},
    y: {label: "stations", grid: true, nice: true, ticks: 3},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: palette.text, strokeOpacity: 0.2}),
      Plot.line(data, {
        x: "day",
        y: "n",
        z: "series",
        curve: "step",
        stroke: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
        strokeWidth: 1.5
      })
    ]
  });
}

// Every chart on this page is built here, in the card that shows it, the
// way the Map and Station cards build theirs. Two separate mechanisms
// require it. An OJS cell's node is inserted where the cell is defined, so
// a chart built in the hidden `output: false` chunk above is adopted by
// that chunk and this panel stays empty. Charts also carry their own width:
// rewrites every `Plot.plot` call to take the width and height of the cell
// the call appears in, so a chart built in that hidden chunk is measured
// against a container that is never visible and comes out 0 px wide.
trendView = {
  // Which chains each country has, so every chart below names a chain by the
  // same rule, and only where a country has two.
  const chains = chainsByCountry(trendCountryRows);

  function allCountriesUsd() {
    const data = trendCountryRows
      .filter((row) => row.median_usd_per_litre != null)
      .map((row) => ({
        country: row.country,
        brand: row.brand,
        // The line's identity is the CHAIN in a country, not the country. Two
        // chains share a country, and a series keyed on country alone would
        // draw one line zig-zagging between two different companies' prices.
        series: row.brand ? `${row.country}-${row.brand}` : row.country,
        label: seriesLabel(row.country, row.brand, chains),
        day: toDay(row.d),
        median: perVolume(row.median_usd_per_litre, volume),
        p25: perVolume(row.p25_usd_per_litre, volume),
        p75: perVolume(row.p75_usd_per_litre, volume)
      }));
    if (!data.length) {
      return html`<div class="cgp-notice">No USD values for ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}.</div>`;
    }
    const days = [...new Set(data.map((row) => row.day.getTime()))].sort();
    const marks = [];
    if (showBand) {
      marks.push(
        Plot.areaY(data, {
          x: "day",
          y1: "p25",
          y2: "p75",
          z: "series",
          fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
          fillOpacity: 0.14
        })
      );
    }
    marks.push(
      Plot.line(data.filter((row) => !row.brand || row.brand === PRIMARY_BRAND), {
        x: "day",
        y: "median",
        z: "series",
        stroke: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
        strokeWidth: 2
      }),
      Plot.line(data.filter((row) => row.brand && row.brand !== PRIMARY_BRAND), {
        x: "day",
        y: "median",
        z: "series",
        stroke: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
        strokeWidth: 2,
        strokeDasharray: "4 3"
      }),
      ...(showDots(days.length)
        ? [Plot.dot(data, {x: "day", y: "median", r: 2, fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country]})]
        : []),
      // selectLast per series, not "rows on the global last day": a country
      // whose feed stalls loses its label under the second rule, and that is
      // exactly the one worth naming. `z` is explicit because `stroke` is a
      // function, and Plot cannot infer the series from it.
      Plot.text(
        data,
        Plot.selectLast({
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          z: "series",
          text: "label",
          dx: 14,
          fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country]
        })
      ),
      // Last, so it paints over the country labels rather than under them.
      Plot.tip(
        data,
        Plot.pointer({
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          ...tipStyle(),
          title: (row) =>
            `${row.label} · ${row.day.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}\n` +
            `median ${fmtNumber(row.median, priceDigits)} USD ${volumeLabel}\n` +
            `p25 ${fmtNumber(row.p25, priceDigits)} · p75 ${fmtNumber(row.p75, priceDigits)}`
        })
      )
    );
    const figure = Plot.plot({
      width: chartWidth,
      ariaLabel: `Median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} price over time, by country`,
      height: 420,
      marginRight: 60,
      style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
      x: {label: "Capture date (UTC)", grid: true, ticks: dayTicks(days)},
      y: {label: `Median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}, USD ${volumeLabel}`, grid: true, nice: true},
      marks
    });
    return html`<div>${figure}${coverageStrip(trendCountryRows, {
      label: GRADE_LABELS[grade]
    })}<div class="cgp-notice">${coverageNote(
      days.length,
      dayText(new Date(days[0])),
      dayText(new Date(days[days.length - 1])),
      latestStationCount(trendCountryRows)
    )}</div></div>`;
  }

  // One chart for every country, in either currency, because what it plots is a
  // ratio of two prices in the same currency. The unit cancels before anything
  // is drawn, so nothing is converted and nothing is compared but the size of a
  // move.
  function allCountriesChange() {
    const byCountry = new Map();
    for (const row of trendCountryRows) {
      const value = perVolume(
        currency === "USD" ? row.median_usd_per_litre : row.median_local_per_litre,
        volume
      );
      if (value == null) continue;
      const seriesKey = row.brand ? `${row.country}-${row.brand}` : row.country;
      if (!byCountry.has(seriesKey)) byCountry.set(seriesKey, []);
      byCountry.get(seriesKey).push({
        country: row.country,
        brand: row.brand,
        day: toDay(row.d),
        value,
        p25: perVolume(
          currency === "USD" ? row.p25_usd_per_litre : row.p25_local_per_litre,
          volume
        ),
        p75: perVolume(
          currency === "USD" ? row.p75_usd_per_litre : row.p75_local_per_litre,
          volume
        )
      });
    }
    const series = [...byCountry.values()];
    const baseDay = commonBaseDay(series);
    if (!baseDay) {
      return html`<div class="cgp-notice">Not enough history yet for
        ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}.</div>`;
    }
    const data = [];
    for (const [code, rows] of byCountry) {
      const anchor = anchorRow(rows, baseDay);
      if (!anchor) continue;
      const rebased = anchor.day.getTime() !== baseDay.getTime();
      for (const row of rows) {
        const pct = pctFrom(row.value, anchor.value);
        if (pct == null) continue;
        data.push({
          country: row.country,
          brand: row.brand,
          series: code,
          label: seriesLabel(row.country, row.brand, chains),
          day: row.day,
          pct,
          p25: pctFrom(row.p25, anchor.value),
          p75: pctFrom(row.p75, anchor.value),
          price: row.value,
          anchorPrice: anchor.value,
          anchorDay: dayText(anchor.day),
          unit: currency === "USD" ? "USD" : currencyOf.get(code) || "local",
          rebased
        });
      }
    }
    if (!data.length) {
      return html`<div class="cgp-notice">No values for ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}.</div>`;
    }
    const baseText = dayText(baseDay);
    const days = [...new Set(data.map((row) => row.day.getTime()))].sort();
    const marks = [Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: palette.grid})];
    if (showBand) {
      marks.push(
        Plot.areaY(
          data.filter((row) => row.p25 != null && row.p75 != null),
          {
            x: "day",
            y1: "p25",
            y2: "p75",
            z: "series",
            fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
            fillOpacity: 0.12
          }
        )
      );
    }
    marks.push(
      Plot.line(data.filter((row) => !row.brand || row.brand === PRIMARY_BRAND), {
        x: "day",
        y: "pct",
        z: "series",
        stroke: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
        strokeWidth: 2
      }),
      Plot.line(data.filter((row) => row.brand && row.brand !== PRIMARY_BRAND), {
        x: "day",
        y: "pct",
        z: "series",
        stroke: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country],
        strokeWidth: 2,
        strokeDasharray: "4 3"
      }),
      ...(showDots(days.length)
        ? [Plot.dot(data, {x: "day", y: "pct", r: 2, fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country]})]
        : []),
      Plot.text(
        data,
        Plot.selectLast({
          x: "day",
          y: "pct",
          z: "series",
          text: "label",
          dx: 14,
          fill: (row) => COUNTRY_COLORS[row.country]
        })
      ),
      Plot.tip(
        data,
        Plot.pointer({
          x: "day",
          y: "pct",
          ...tipStyle(),
          title: (row) =>
            `${row.label} · ${dayText(row.day)}\n` +
            `${fmtPct(row.pct)} since ${row.anchorDay}${
              row.rebased ? " (its own first day)" : ""
            }\n` +
            `${fmtNumber(row.price, priceDigits)} ${row.unit}${volumeShort} that day\n` +
            `${fmtNumber(row.anchorPrice, priceDigits)} ${row.unit}${volumeShort} on ${
              row.anchorDay
            }`
        })
      )
    );
    const label =
      currency === "USD"
        ? `Change in median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} since ${baseText}, in USD (%)`
        : `Change in median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} since ${baseText}, each country in its own currency (%)`;
    const figure = Plot.plot({
      width: chartWidth,
      ariaLabel: `Change in median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} since ${baseText}, by country`,
      height: 400,
      marginRight: 60,
      style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
      x: {label: "Capture date (UTC)", grid: true, ticks: dayTicks(days)},
      y: {label, grid: true, nice: true, tickFormat: fmtPct},
      marks
    });
    return html`<div>${figure}${coverageStrip(trendCountryRows, {
      label: GRADE_LABELS[grade]
    })}<div class="cgp-notice">${coverageNote(
      days.length,
      dayText(new Date(days[0])),
      dayText(new Date(days[days.length - 1])),
      latestStationCount(trendCountryRows)
    )}</div></div>`;
  }

  function allCountriesLocal() {
    const byCountry = new Map();
    for (const row of trendCountryRows) {
      if (row.median_local_per_litre == null) continue;
      if (!byCountry.has(row.country)) byCountry.set(row.country, []);
      byCountry.get(row.country).push({
        country: row.country,
        brand: row.brand,
        series: row.brand ? `${row.country}-${row.brand}` : row.country,
        day: toDay(row.d),
        median: perVolume(row.median_local_per_litre, volume),
        p25: perVolume(row.p25_local_per_litre, volume),
        p75: perVolume(row.p75_local_per_litre, volume)
      });
    }
    const panels = COUNTRY_ORDER.filter((code) => byCountry.has(code)).map((code) => {
      const rows = byCountry.get(code);
      const marks = [];
      if (showBand) {
        marks.push(
          // One band per chain. Without `z` the two chains' rows became one
          // polygon that ran to the last day and doubled back over the first.
          Plot.areaY(rows, {
            x: "day",
            y1: "p25",
            y2: "p75",
            z: "series",
            fill: COUNTRY_COLORS[code],
            fillOpacity: 0.16
          })
        );
      }
      const unit = `${currencyOf.get(code) || ""} ${volumeShort}`;
      marks.push(
        Plot.line(rows.filter((r) => !r.brand || r.brand === PRIMARY_BRAND), {
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          z: "series",
          stroke: COUNTRY_COLORS[code],
          strokeWidth: 2
        }),
        Plot.line(rows.filter((r) => r.brand && r.brand !== PRIMARY_BRAND), {
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          z: "series",
          stroke: COUNTRY_COLORS[code],
          strokeWidth: 2,
          strokeDasharray: "4 3"
        }),
        Plot.dot(rows, {x: "day", y: "median", r: 2, fill: COUNTRY_COLORS[code]}),
        Plot.tip(
          rows,
          Plot.pointerX({
            x: "day",
            y: "median",
            ...tipStyle(),
            title: (row) =>
              `${seriesLabel(code, row.brand, chains)} · ${dayText(row.day)}\n` +
              `median ${fmtNumber(row.median, priceDigits)} ${unit}\n` +
              `p25 ${fmtNumber(row.p25, priceDigits)} · p75 ${fmtNumber(row.p75, priceDigits)}`
          })
        )
      );
      const figure = Plot.plot({
        // A panel, not the card: without an explicit width Quarto's autosizing
        // gives every one of these the full card width, and the
        // `.cgp-small-multiples` grid (columns of at least 240 px) collapses
        // to a single column. An explicit width wins because the injected one
        // is prepended to this object.
        width: 240,
        ariaLabel: `${COUNTRY_NAMES[code] || code}: median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} over time, ${unit}`,
        height: 190,
        marginLeft: 52,
        style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
        x: {label: null, ticks: 4, grid: true},
        y: {label: `${currencyOf.get(code) || ""} ${volumeShort}`, grid: true, nice: true},
        marks
      });
      return html`<div><div class="cgp-stale">${COUNTRY_NAMES[code]}</div>${figure}</div>`;
    });
    if (!panels.length) {
      return html`<div class="cgp-notice">No local values for ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}.</div>`;
    }
    return html`<div class="cgp-small-multiples">${panels}</div>`;
  }

  function regionBreakdown() {
    const unit = currency === "USD" ? "USD" : currencyOf.get(trendCountry) || "local";
    if (!trendRegionOptions.length) {
      const rows = trendCountryRows
        .filter((row) => row.country === trendCountry)
        .map((row) => ({
          // Per chain, as on every other chart here, should a country without
          // regions ever have two.
          series: seriesOf(row),
          label: seriesLabel(row.country, row.brand, chains),
          day: toDay(row.d),
          median: perVolume(
            currency === "USD" ? row.median_usd_per_litre : row.median_local_per_litre,
            volume
          )
        }))
        .filter((row) => row.median != null);
      const figure = Plot.plot({
        width: chartWidth,
        ariaLabel: `${COUNTRY_NAMES[trendCountry] || trendCountry}: median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} over time`,
        height: 400,
        style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
        x: {label: "Capture date (UTC)", grid: true, ticks: dayTicks(rows)},
        y: {label: `Median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}, ${unit} ${volumeLabel}`, grid: true, nice: true},
        marks: [
          Plot.line(rows, {
            x: "day",
            y: "median",
            z: "series",
            stroke: COUNTRY_COLORS[trendCountry],
            strokeWidth: 2
          }),
          Plot.dot(rows, {x: "day", y: "median", r: 2, fill: COUNTRY_COLORS[trendCountry]}),
          Plot.tip(
            rows,
            Plot.pointerX({
              x: "day",
              y: "median",
              ...tipStyle(),
              title: (row) =>
                `${row.label} · ${row.day.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}\n` +
                `median ${fmtNumber(row.median, priceDigits)} ${unit} ${volumeLabel}`
            })
          )
        ]
      });
      return html`<div>
        <div class="cgp-notice">No regional breakdown for ${COUNTRY_NAMES[trendCountry]};
          showing the national series.</div>
        ${figure}
      </div>`;
    }
    // tableau10 has ten colors. Asked for more series than that, Plot cycles
    // them silently and the legend then claims two regions are one -- five US
    // states would share every color. Cap the drawn set and say so, rather than
    // drawing a key that is not true.
    const asked = trendRegions;
    const drawn = asked.slice(0, PALETTE_SERIES_CAP);
    const chosen = new Set(drawn);
    // A region with two chains is two lines, the way a country is: keyed on the
    // region alone, one line zig-zagged between the two companies' prices. Both
    // take the region's color, and the second chain is dashed.
    const brands = chains.get(trendCountry) || new Set();
    const data = trendRegionRows
      .filter((row) => chosen.has(row.region))
      .map((row) => ({
        region: row.region,
        brand: row.brand,
        series: `${row.region} :: ${row.brand}`,
        label: placeLabel(row.region, trendCountry, row.brand, chains),
        day: toDay(row.d),
        median: perVolume(
          currency === "USD" ? row.median_usd_per_litre : row.median_local_per_litre,
          volume
        )
      }))
      .filter((row) => row.median != null);
    if (!data.length) return html`<div class="cgp-notice">Pick at least one region.</div>`;
    const figure = Plot.plot({
      width: chartWidth,
      ariaLabel: `${COUNTRY_NAMES[trendCountry] || trendCountry}: median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]} by region`,
      height: 420,
      marginRight: 80,
      style: {background: "transparent", color: palette.text},
      // Quarto's OJS stdlib pins Plot 0.6.11, which has no `observable10`
      // ordinal scheme: naming it throws and turns the whole cell into an error.
      color: {legend: true, scheme: "tableau10"},
      x: {label: "Capture date (UTC)", grid: true, ticks: dayTicks(data)},
      y: {label: `Median ${GRADE_LABELS[grade]}, ${unit} ${volumeLabel}`, grid: true, nice: true},
      marks: [
        Plot.line(data.filter((row) => !row.brand || row.brand === PRIMARY_BRAND), {
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          z: "series",
          stroke: "region",
          strokeWidth: 2
        }),
        Plot.line(data.filter((row) => row.brand && row.brand !== PRIMARY_BRAND), {
          x: "day",
          y: "median",
          z: "series",
          stroke: "region",
          strokeWidth: 2,
          strokeDasharray: "4 3"
        }),
        Plot.dot(data, {x: "day", y: "median", r: 2, fill: "region"}),
        Plot.tip(
          data,
          Plot.pointer({
            x: "day",
            y: "median",
            ...tipStyle(),
            title: (row) =>
              `${row.label} · ${row.day.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}\n` +
              `median ${fmtNumber(row.median, priceDigits)} ${unit} ${volumeLabel}`
          })
        )
      ]
    });
    // The color legend is spent on regions, so which line is which chain
    // needs a key of its own -- only where there are two to tell apart.
    const key = brands.size > 1 ? chainKeyEl(brands) : "";
    if (asked.length <= drawn.length && !key) return figure;
    const capped =
      asked.length <= drawn.length
        ? ""
        : html`<div class="cgp-notice">Showing the first
      ${drawn.length} of ${asked.length} regions you picked: the palette has
      ${PALETTE_SERIES_CAP} colors, and beyond that two regions would share
      one. Separate charts shows them all.</div>`;
    return html`<div>${key}${figure}${capped}</div>`;
  }

  if (!db) return html`<div class="cgp-notice">Loading the price database…</div>`;
  if (effectiveTrendMode === "separate") {
    return trendCountry === "All countries" ? allCountriesLocal() : regionBreakdown();
  }
  if (effectiveTrendMode === "change") return allCountriesChange();
  return trendCountry === "All countries" ? allCountriesUsd() : regionBreakdown();
}
```
